body.statement: If \(K=2\), \(q=(1,0)^{\top}\), and \(T\ge4\), then \(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}\in\mathfrak D_T\), \(\mathbb E_{D_T^{\mathrm{iid}}}[S_T^2]=T-1\), and \(\mathcal R_T(D_T^{\mathrm{iid}})=\max\{R_e^2,(T-1)R_g^2/T\}\). Therefore independent Rademacher assignment is minimax if and only if \(R_e^2/R_g^2\ge(T-1)/T\); below this threshold its excess normalized MSE is \((T-1)R_g^2/T-\max\{R_e^2,a_TR_g^2/T\}>0\).
body.justification: The corollary gives the exact signal-to-disturbance frontier at which unrestricted fourth-order design ceases to improve on independent toggling.
body.gap: Guo and Liang obtain asymptotic iid optimality for an E-optimal OLS information criterion within structured switching families; this finite threshold instead concerns worst-case fixed-path MSE of the displayed unbiased moment estimator over every pairwise-orthogonal law.
body.consumer: A trial designer can decide from \(R_e^2/R_g^2\) whether iid toggling is certified or whether the mirrored law yields a strict finite-horizon gain.
